records.subject: Getting started with Wrenfield
records.body:
Hi Ana,

Welcome to Wrenfield. There's no wrong way to start -- create a project, add a few tasks, invite people, and adjust as you figure out what works for your team.

Reply here if you need a hand.

Best,
Nadia Goldberg

decisions.rationale: Engaged, friendly reply [email:fceedcfb] but deferred the walkthrough ("at some point") and took no action after two touches [email:b7929bbf, email:8e0ce85d]: 6 days in with no project, no invite, no tickets. Pro plan and responsiveness suggest some intent, but momentum is absent with 8 days left.

draft.subject: Re: A few days into Wrenfield -- how's it going?
draft.body:
Hi Ana,

Thanks for the note -- glad things are going well so far, and the offer of a walkthrough stands whenever you want it.

Whenever you're ready to start, projects are the main organizing unit in Wrenfield, and tasks live inside them, so a first project is usually the easiest place to begin. The in-app onboarding flow walks through creating a first project. When you want teammates in there, a teammate can be invited from Account Settings -> Members at any time.

Would a short call this week suit? Happy to work through your first project together.

Best,
Nadia
